doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Scat-singing through the flute and Jake Hanna's Buddy Rich story
summary: He began singing while playing in a closet and on the subway; Jake Hanna's exaggerated tale of his late entrance with Rich.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: When did the idea of singing through the flute start for you?

There’s a little story involved with that. I couldn’t make a lot of noise in my apartment. I was living with my folks, and so I used to go in the closet and just [scats]. I’d sing while I was playing, because I wouldn’t have to play the notes at full volume, something like that. People told me I used to practice on the subway, you know take out the flute and everything. I don’t remember some of these crazy things you do when you’re young.
Yeah. People tell you you did though.
I did, yeah. “Remember you used to take out the flute and play some bebop on the subway” or something. Because as I say I couldn’t make a lot of noise, maybe it was late
at night and I wanted to play something so that’s how that happened. Then I guess I recorded with it. And one of the earliest as far as I cam remember.
Well Jake Hanna made up, he tells a story about you making this weird entrance—

Oh yeah. He loves to tell that and no one could seem to tell it like him. We were playing at the Maryland Hotel in Chicago. And he builds up the story, he says, “And now, ladies and gentlemen, Buddy Rich, the world’s greatest drummer.” It’s pitch black. And then he says, “And guess what happens” he says I’m late for the stage, and he says, “and here comes Sam running to get on the stage on time.” “Now the world’s greatest drummer.” I knock over his cymbals and the whole bass drum and everything falls to the floor.” The world’s greatest drummer. And he fires me, and that’s the story.
Is there any truth to it?
No. Maybe some, maybe I hit the cymbal or something or came in late.
Gee, there should be some truth to it anyway, at least to elaborate on it, he’s got to start somewhere.
Yeah, there must be some truth but he exaggerates, but he tells it wonderfully.
